about: The error codes gglib writes itself, rather than relays from llama-server, on its proxy and the daemon's runs. The proxy refuses with {"error":{"message":...,"type":...,"code":...}}, and a stream already under way can end with that object as a data: frame. A run that failed carries {"code":...,"message":...} as its error, on /v1/runs and /api/runs. The daemon's /api/runs refuses with {"error":...,"status":...,"type":<code>}, and the proxy answers a paired device's turn on a hub chat with the daemon's refusal of it. The daemon's guards in front of /api refuse with upper-case types of their own, such as HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, which are not listed here. Match on code. type is the type the proxy writes beside the code: null where it writes more than one, or none. status is the HTTP status of every response that carries the code: null where those responses' writers do not all fix the same one, or where no response carries it, only a stream frame or a run's error.

codes.meaning: The model is still loading; retry shortly.
The request waited its limit for the model without being admitted; retry shortly.
No model with that id or name is in the catalog.
No model has that name, and its :suffix names no inference profile.
An embeddings request named a model not tagged embedding.
A chat request named an embedding model.
A message carries an image and the model has no projector linked; link one with gglib model update <model> --projector <path>.
The request body is over the 32 MiB limit.
An uploaded image is over the 8 MiB one image may be.
An uploaded file is not a PNG or a JPEG whose size can be read.
A message names an image id that is not stored (400), or an image was asked for by an id that is not stored (404); upload the image again.
The images a chat's messages carry, history included, are over the 16 MiB one request to a model may carry; the run is refused before it starts. Start a new chat, or send fewer or smaller images.
The model server (for a run, the proxy) failed, could not be reached, or ended a reply early; the type beside it may be llama-server's.
The conversation does not fit the model's context even trimmed; start a new one.
The history repeats the same tool calls with the same results, so the request was refused or the agent run stopped.
The assistant gave the same reply too often, so the request was refused or the agent run stopped.
The request could not be read or is not valid.
gglib failed on its own side; the message says where.
The model is in the catalog but its file is missing.
This endpoint serves one pinned model, and the request named another.
The Host is neither loopback nor a host allowed with --allowed-host.
A page on another site sent a change.
The bearer token is missing or wrong.
A request came through the tunnel without a paired device's key.
This machine does not open its MCP gateway to the tunnel.
The route serves a paired device through the tunnel, and the request did not name one.
This proxy runs outside the gglib daemon, so it holds no runs.
This proxy runs outside the gglib daemon, so it holds no chats.
Nothing with that id is visible to the caller.
The run id is taken, the conversation already has a live reply, or a run or a device's turn names a chat that ran on another machine.
The run belongs to a paired device, so only that device may read its reply.
Too many runs are still going; cancel one or wait.
The daemon is stopping, so it starts no more runs.
No conversation has that id.
Every agent loop slot is in use; retry later.
The chat names no model and nothing is running on the hub.
The chat's model could not be loaded on the hub.
Something the run needs is unavailable, such as a model stopped while the run was prepared; retry.
The message a run was to replace is not in its conversation.
The model server sent nothing, or did not finish, within its time limit; retry.
The run stopped on an internal failure.
The proxy was not running, so the chat run had nowhere to go.
The reply passed the 8 MB a run may hold.
The agent reached its iteration limit without a final answer.
The model asked for more tool calls at once than are allowed.
The agent loop failed; the run's last event says why.
The reply could not be saved to its conversation.
